newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count up 8 to 827 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count up 8 to 827 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 827 as of Oct. 11, up eight from the prior week and 64 above the year-ago total of 763, Baker Hughes Inc. reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by 11 to 701, while rigs working offshore fell by 12 to 102. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose by nine to 24.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in Texas, which showed a decrease of 10, and Oklahoma, which showed an increase of eight. New Mexico rose by six.

A total of 347 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up 36 from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas fell by 28 to 475, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained unchanged at five.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by four to 259 vs. 209 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 166 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Oct. 11, unchanged from the prior week.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 180, was 92.2 percent.
The number of working rigs in European/Mediterranean rose by one this week to 105 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 105, a utilization rate of 100 percent.
The worldwide rig count felly by two to 560 out of a total fleet of 604, making the utilization rate 92.7 percent.
